AI use in game
I am struggling to find a way to contact the Lost Pixel team, but I had wishlisted this game a few weeks ago and was looking forward to playing it, only to find out that many of the gameplay elements were generated with AI. I am disappointed and will not be purchasing the game, but I do want to encourage the team to remake the game without relying on AI and I want to encourage consumers to be weary of AI-heavy games and products, especially in the "cozy" genre. AI is something that consumers are weary of and it can absolutely damage the reputation of indie game developers.

At least OP has had the stones to post on their proper account. Most of these "AI bad - will not buy" posts come from obvious second accounts (Steam level 0 - no games in library etc,) and you just know that their actual account is probably brimming with tidy-up games full of "slop".

At the end of the day - you want your tidy-up game to cost under a fiver? Then you're probably going to have to accept a certain amount of AI use. It costs money to list a game on Steam and they take a significant cut of each sale too but the Anti-Ai mob don't take this into consideration. I'm sure they have visions of an artist starving in a garret while the developer of Tidy-up the Latest Thing is rolling around on a bed covered in Benjamins. It's just not the case.

Having said all that, Kimari has a point - if keyboards are showing keys that don't exist in reality then something needs to be done and the fact that nothing was done before release show that these particular devs DGAF. The devs of all the tidy-up games I buy are usually bending over backwards to fix issues and problems and that's why I bought their game in the first place - I check the discussion board before making a decision and if a dev shows that they care about their game and are making sure it's the best it can be, then I can forgive a bit of AI.
